subject: Dedicated Sizing & Burst Policy for TideScale — next steps
messages:

Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity + burst for launch week

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. We are aiming for a staged public release the week of July 19 and expect a short-term surge during the 72-hour launch window. A few quick items we need from Redwood to finalize our procurement plan: 

- Recommended dedicated GPU slab for our steady-state inference for a 13B-conversational model (typical seq len ~512).
- Burst strategy: how many ephemeral GPUs can you support for a 3-day surge and what the failover looks like if capacity is limited?
- Warm-up/pre-warm requirements and expected time to full throughput if we bring ephemeral nodes online.
- Pricing model for reserved + burst (hourly vs per-token for burst).

We need to present an internal SOC/ops runbook to our CTO and procurement by July 9. Can you send an initial sizing + policy proposal and an estimate of cost impact for the launch?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 14:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity + burst for launch week — proposed autoscale policy

Hi Elena / Sean,

Attaching a draft capacity proposal (tidescale_capacity_proposal_v1.pdf) and a detailed autoscale matrix (ts_autoscale_matrix.xlsx). Highlights below so the runbook is easy to extract: 

- Baseline (reserved): 8x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs for steady-state. That supports ~180 qps at 512 tokens with our optimized kernels and continuous batching.
- Burst pool (ephemeral): +12 GPUs available for burst (can scale up to +20 if we set a higher ceiling). Ephemeral GPUs are billed hourly and can be pre-warmed.
- Headroom policy: maintain 25% headroom on baseline for sudden spikes; trigger ephemeral scale when queue latency > 150ms for >30s.
- Pre-warm policy: optional pre-warm when projected surge >50% above baseline. Pre-warm actions: launch ephemeral nodes 60 minutes pre-launch, warm KV cache using synthetic warm-up traffic (we can run warm-up scripts). Expected warm-up to full throughput: ~18-45 minutes depending on model kv-cache size.
- Eviction & preemption: ephemeral GPUs are preemptible; if capacity constrained, traffic is routed to a lower-cost quantized variant (13B-int8) automatically. We can set a hard burst ceiling and a soft ceiling with graceful degradation.
- SLA considerations: for the 72-hour launch we recommend enabling a temporary higher-priority burst pool (non-preemptible) for the first 6 hours of each launch day — this requires reserved short-term capacity and a separate addendum.

Estimated impact on cost (very rough):
- Baseline monthly: reserved slab cost (8x) = ~$86k/month (discounted commited rate).
- Burst: hourly ephemeral rate ~ $12/hr per GPU; 12 GPUs over 72 hrs -> ~ $12 * 12 * 72 = $10,368 (before any negotiated burst discount). If you go to 20 GPUs peak: ~$17,280.

Operational runbook snippets included in the PDF: warm-up commands, health-check endpoints, tracing flags to validate KV cache warm acceptance, and a quick rollback (fallback to quantized variant) if error rates rise.

Next steps I'd propose:
1) Elena: confirm peak qps estimate and any no-preempt windows.
2) Agreement on burst ceiling (12 vs 20 GPUs).
3) Lauren: finalize pricing + addendum.
4) We schedule a pre-warm dry-run on your staging cluster a week before launch.

Ben Carter
Principal Infra Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: tidescale_capacity_proposal_v1.pdf; ts_autoscale_matrix.xlsx

Couple of commercial points aligned with Ben’s technical plan: 

- Offer: Reserved slab (8x GPUs) on a 12-month commitment + a capped burst pool. We can cap burst billable hours for the 72-hour launch to 120 GPU-hours at a discounted rate (30% off list) as a one-time concession for this launch.
- Addendum: temporary non-preemptible mini-pool for the first 6 hours each launch day (as Ben noted) — priced as hourly reserved at a short-term rate.
- Procurement: we can put the burst cap and the addendum into the SOW. I'll prepare a draft SOW and route it via DocuSign once you confirm the ceiling.
